title: Economic Fury Targets Global Network Fueling Iran's Oil Trade and Shadow Fleet
summary: OFAC sanctioned China's second-largest teapot refinery Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co., Ltd. and approximately 40 shipping firms and vessels as part of the 'Economic Fury' campaign targeting Iran's oil export infrastructure. The sanctions target Iran's shadow fleet and major customers to constrict Tehran's oil revenue, which Treasury says funds regional aggression and nuclear ambitions.
key_points: Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery is China's second-largest independent teapot refinery and one of Iran's largest customers for crude oil and petroleum products, purchasing billions of dollars' worth since at least 2023
Over 1,000 Iran-related persons, vessels, and aircraft have been sanctioned since February 2025 under the Economic Fury campaign

Sanctioned vessels include LISBOA (2.5 million barrels Iranian naphtha to UAE, July 2025-January 2026), SEVAN (750,000 barrels Iranian LPG to Bangladesh, August-November 2025), and SEEKER 8 (4+ million barrels to China, January-February 2026)
Several vessels engaged in ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian crude oil off Malaysia's coast to evade detection
Actions taken pursuant to Executive Order 13902 and NSPM-2 targeting Iran's petroleum sector and sanctions evasion networks
Four teapot refineries previously targeted as part of President Trump's maximum pressure campaign
why_it_matters: These sanctions directly target the infrastructure Iran uses to sell oil, which funds the regime's military activities in the Middle East. By restricting access to China's teapot refineries and the shadow fleet, the U.S. aims to cut Iran's oil revenue. This creates supply disruption risk for global oil markets and increases shipping costs through tighter enforcement on vessel routes.
macro_context: Sanctions on Iran's oil export infrastructure represent a significant escalation in maximum pressure campaign. If enforced effectively, these actions could remove substantial Iranian crude from global markets, tightening supply. The targeting of Chinese teapot refineries—responsible for the majority of Iran's crude sales—indicates willingness to impose secondary sanctions on Chinese entities, which could have broader geopolitical implications.
important_numbers: 40 shipping firms and vessels sanctioned in this action
5+ million barrels delivered by shadow fleet vessels BIG MAG, GALE, and ARES
